_comment: Operator-editable shop settings. No secrets here — credentials live in ops/worker/.env (gitignored). Run `node ops.mjs` any time to see which of these still needs your attention.
shop_name_note: The exact Etsy shop name. It is printed in every listing description as the 'Designed by' attribution, so it must match the real shop. Set it before running: node ops.mjs listings

processing._comment: Shipping speed is a promise, and a broken one voids Etsy Purchase Protection and costs Star Seller status. So it is blank until you know the real number. `node ops.mjs plan` prints the resolved provider's published production time; add carrier transit on top, put the result here, name where it came from in `source`, and only then does it appear in listing descriptions.

min_margin_note: Net profit per unit after Printify base cost AND the fee schedule below. `node ops.mjs stage` deletes any draft that comes back under this — it will not leave a money-loser sitting in the shop.
max_products_note: Runaway guard for ONE invocation. A single stage run can never create more than this many products, no matter what the listing file says.
max_products_total_note: Runaway guard across ALL invocations. Before creating anything, stage counts the products that actually exist in the Printify shop and refuses if this run would push the total past this. A loop calling stage repeatedly dies on the second call, not the two-hundredth product.

fees._source: Etsy's published seller fee schedule. NOT fetched from an API — you must confirm these against your own Etsy account (Shop Manager → Finances → Payment settings) because rates vary by country, currency, and whether Offsite Ads is mandatory for your shop.
fees._confirm: Set fees_confirmed to true once you have checked these against your own account. Until then margin numbers are printed but marked UNCONFIRMED, and publish refuses to run.
fees.offsite_ads_note: Etsy charges 12% (or 15%) only on orders that came from an Offsite Ad. Leave at 0 for a per-unit floor; raise it if you want the margin guard to survive the worst case.
fees.free_shipping_note: false = the buyer pays shipping, so it passes straight through to Printify and does not touch margin. Set true only if you offer free shipping — then the margin guard pulls the REAL first-item US shipping rate from Printify and subtracts it, and refuses to stage anything if Printify will not give it that number.
